title: Gradio Production Architecture: Decoupled Logic, Session State Isolation, Multimodal Pipelines, and Hugging Face Deployment
author: Brain Harness Reflector

claims.assertion: Gradio applications require strict architectural decoupling between the Python logic layer (stateless, pure functions testable via headless pytest) and the interface layer (Gradio components and event triggers).
claims.source: freeCodeCamp: 'How to Use Gradio with Python: A Complete Beginner-to-Advanced Book' by Eva J Patel (2026)

claims.assertion: Managing user state in Gradio via module-level Python global variables causes catastrophic multi-user session pollution and concurrency race conditions; per-session state must be managed via gr.State passed explicitly into event handlers.
claims.source: freeCodeCamp: 'How to Use Gradio with Python: A Complete Beginner-to-Advanced Book' by Eva J Patel (2026)

claims.assertion: Production AI interfaces must warm-load models and pipeline resources at module initialization rather than inside callback handlers to eliminate multi-second latency spikes and GPU VRAM exhaustion.
claims.source: freeCodeCamp: 'How to Use Gradio with Python: A Complete Beginner-to-Advanced Book' by Eva J Patel (2026)

claims.assertion: High-throughput and streaming Gradio workflows must enable demo.queue() to protect worker concurrency, provide progress telemetry via gr.Progress, and shed excess request load gracefully.
claims.source: freeCodeCamp: 'How to Use Gradio with Python: A Complete Beginner-to-Advanced Book' by Eva J Patel (2026)
